name: v1_default
_comment_models: 42 models total: the 30 TabArena-native models onboarded/wired this session (16 previously-listed-but-unwired, fixed in 5c57fe4, plus 14 newly onboarded in 3 batches: 98c44ad/90f49a8/a6a6986) plus 11 pre-existing RamanBench-native custom architectures verified against the v1 pipeline in a separate follow-up (aae8393: ARSENAL, COATNET, DEEPCNN, FCRESNEXT, RAMANFORMER, RAMANNET, RAMANTRANSFORMER, REZERONET, ROCKET, SANET, plus TABPFN-WIDE re-added after aae8393 fixed a real CPU-fallback bug -- device was hardcoded 'cpu' despite info.py tagging compute='gpu', so it silently never used the GPU it was allocated). All 42 confirmed to resolve cleanly via raman_bench.models.registry.infer_model_cls. PLS is listed LAST, not first: pick_chunk() picks the FIRST model in this list with a nonempty backlog and takes a full chunk_size from it before ever looking at the next model (strict priority, not round-robin) -- PLS already has a large in-progress backlog from its long head start, so putting it first would starve every other model of new submissions until PLS's backlog was fully drained. PLS's own already-queued/running SLURM tasks are unaffected by this ordering (only NEW chunk submissions go through pick_chunk). The 11 custom architectures have no existing production backlog, so their relative order doesn't matter much; placed after the 30 TabArena models (which were dry-run-verified first) and still ahead of PLS. Deliberately still excludes AUTOGLUON only (whole-predictor meta-preset, not a per-model ConfigGenerator -- can't be wired into run_experiment.py's one-model-per-job design as-is; GBM was never part of either onboarding effort and stays out until its own verification pass). WATCH ITEM: TABPFN-WIDE's GPU fix (aae8393) was verified functionally correct but the actual speedup was NOT confirmed on real hardware (the dev machine fixing it had no CUDA) -- watch its first real runs, especially against the 3 large classification datasets it's eligible for (mlrod 130,061 rows, bacteria_identification 78,500 rows, wheat_lines 53,134 rows); mlrod already gets the blanket 10800s dataset-level override below, but if CUDA doesn't actually get exercised in the real SLURM allocation for any reason, a naive linear extrapolation from aae8393's own CPU-only scaling probe (20 rows->5.7s, 350 rows->88.2s) suggests even that 10800s budget could plausibly be too small at mlrod's full scale -- no override added preemptively since this is speculative extrapolation over a ~370x range, not calibration evidence; add one if a real run confirms it's needed, same convention as EBM/ORIONMSP below.
_comment_model_time_limit_overrides: EBM's real TimeLimitExceeded on wide datasets was mostly interpret's own O(n_features^2) interaction-ranking pre-scan (see Prep_EBM._fit's docstring) -- fixed at the model level (interactions=0 above 4000 features), not by budget alone. A real calibration run post-fix (microgel_synthesis, 11084 features, run_experiment.py --model EBM --time-limit 900 --num-bag-folds 8, auto-scaled to 2 effective folds for this 14-row dataset) finished in 426s wall time (400s training), already well inside the 3600s default. These 5400s entries are headroom, not a required fix: the other 9 targets in the same 11084-11689-feature cluster have more rows and so use the full 8 bag folds (not 2), extrapolating to roughly 4x -> ~1700s -- 5400s leaves >3x margin over that for a slower cluster CPU than the one calibrated on. ORIONMSP's pharmaceutical_ingredients entry is similarly a safety margin, not the primary fix -- see cluster/profiles/htw.yaml's ORIONMSP mem_tier: a real local run there (2 bag folds) finished fitting in ~175s but then crashed from memory (~25-27GB RSS on a 36GB machine), i.e. this dataset's real confirmed risk is memory, not time. LR's entry is a bare number (not a dataset-keyed dict) -- a blanket override applied regardless of dataset (see cluster/submit_job.py::resolve_time_limit's scalar-override handling). Confirmed real: LR's bagged fold fit on wheat_lines/bacteria_identification takes ~530-560s/fold x 8 sequential folds (~4240-4480s), past the 3600s default, so AutoGluon's fold-fitting strategy extrapolated from an early fold and aborted with TimeLimitExceeded before the (finite, just slower-than-guessed) remaining folds got a chance -- same failure mode already seen for PLS on mlrod, just not yet hit for LR until these two datasets. Under the routine config_index=0 backlog (no HPO search opted in), a time cap on a model like LR doesn't bound anything meaningful -- it only risks this same early-abort happening again on some other not-yet-encountered (model, dataset) pair. 800000s (~9.3 days) is comfortably under the real backstop, the SLURM array's own --time (the profile's default_time, 10 days) -- independent of this value.
